BioPharm Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the BioPharm Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by one. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BioPharm Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer; and Karen Lee, Head of Commercial.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of BioPharm Therapeutics.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. BioPharm Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by continued momentum in our GLP-1 obesity franchise and oncology portfolio. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including robust product revenue growth across our key drug franchises, advancements in regulatory approvals and label expansions, disciplined operating expense management, strategic R&D investments and pipeline priorities, navigation of the pricing and reimbursement landscape, and careful consideration of key assumptions and risk factors.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and these strategic initiatives. We are particularly excited about BPT-401, our differentiated oral GLP-1, and its potential to capture meaningful share in the rapidly expanding obesity market through superior patient adherence and our AI-optimized support programs.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $3.2 billion, an increase of 16% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 17% growth in our oncology franchise, strong volume uptake in GLP-1s led by BPT-401, and label expansions across immuno-oncology and rare diseases.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.20 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $520 million, or $1.40 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.5 billion, reflecting continued investments in our late-stage pipeline offset by efficiencies in SG&A and targeted cost optimizations. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $4.8 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to net product sales of $12 to $13 billion, with adjusted operating expenses growing 15 to 17% and non-GAAP EPS of $5.10 to $5.30.

Let me dive deeper into our Q3 product revenue performance, broken out by our three core franchises: oncology, immunology, and rare diseases and gene therapies. Overall, net product sales reached $2.85 billion in the quarter, up 14% year-over-year and 5% sequentially from Q2. This reflects a healthy mix of volume-driven growth from label expansions and new launches, partially offset by pricing headwinds in mature markets like immunology due to biosimilar competition and payer mix shifts. Ex-manufacturing revenue—primarily royalties and milestones—added another $120 million, up 22% year-over-year.

Our oncology franchise delivered $1.65 billion, up 17% year-over-year and representing 58% of total product revenue. Led by our blockbuster PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor OncoVita, which has generated over $5 billion in trailing twelve-month sales, this portfolio continues to be our growth engine. U.S. sales hit $1.2 billion, or 73% of the franchise, with ex-U.S. at $450 million. Volumes increased 13% year-over-year to 285,000 patient-months equivalent, driven by a 20% ramp in new prescriptions following FDA approval of the adjuvant NSCLC indication in Q1. Total prescriptions market share expanded to 28% in first-line metastatic NSCLC, gaining two share points from competitors like Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo, per IQVIA data. In Europe, EMA label alignment and NICE reimbursement in the UK added 8% sequential volume growth, while emerging markets, particularly China via our Sinopharm partnership, contributed 15% year-over-year volume uplift from the recent CFDA approval. Pricing-wise, U.S. ASP rose 4% year-over-year to $5,800 per patient-month, supported by a 6% WAC increase in January, though gross-to-net adjustments widened to 48% from 45% due to higher 340B discounts—now 35% of U.S. volume—and PBM rebates amid initial Inflation Reduction Act impacts. Ex-U.S. ASP was flat at $4,200, pressured by HTA negotiations in Germany and France. We're scaling our Redwood City fill-finish facility by 30% capacity next year to support OncoVita's subcutaneous formulation trial data, expected in the first half of 2025, which could drive another 10 to 15% volume acceleration. Market share in combo regimens with our next-gen ADC, BPT-205 VitaTox, is building, with early combo data boosting new Rx by 25% in triple-negative breast cancer.

The immunology franchise contributed $850 million, up 6% year-over-year and 30% of total product revenue. Anchored by our IL-23 inhibitor Inflamara, competing in psoriasis and Crohn's like AbbVie's Skyrizi, U.S. sales were $620 million, or 73%, with ex-U.S. at $230 million. Volumes grew 8% to 210,000 patient-months, fueled by a 12% new Rx increase in ulcerative colitis post-Phase 3 readout and label expansion, though sequential growth slowed to 2% as biosimilar erosion from Amgen's versions of legacy TNFs intensified, leading to an estimated 5% total Rx share loss in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. In Japan, our Astellas partnership drove 18% volume growth via JPY reimbursement tiers. ASP declined 2% year-over-year to $4,100 per patient-month in the U.S., reflecting rebate inflation to 52% gross-to-net, up from 49%, driven by Express Scripts and CVS Caremark formulary repositioning—we absorbed a 3% list price freeze to maintain preferred status. Ex-U.S., ASP held steady at $3,500, bolstered by volume-based tenders in Brazil and Australia. Looking ahead, our bispecific IL-17/IL-23 candidate in Phase 2 could disrupt this space if it succeeds on efficacy in hidradenitis suppurativa, and we're optimizing our U.S. patient services hub to improve adherence, targeting a 5% total Rx uplift.

Our rare diseases and gene therapies franchise saw $350 million, up 42% year-over-year and 12% of total product revenue. Led by our AAV-based gene therapy RariGene for spinal muscular atrophy, similar to Novartis' Zolgensma, and the recent launch of HemoCure for hemophilia B, U.S. sales dominated at $260 million, or 74%, with ex-U.S. at $90 million. Volumes surged 35% to 1,200 treatment equivalents, primarily from HemoCure's U.S. launch last Q4 with 450 doses infused and RariGene's expansion into older SMA patients, Type II/III. New Rx penetration hit 40% in eligible hemophilia B neonates per NESTcc registry data. In Europe, EMA approval and Italian reimbursement added 25% sequential growth, though China delays limited emerging market volumes to 10% of the franchise. ASP remained premium at $2.1 million per treatment for RariGene, flat year-over-year, and $1.8 million for HemoCure, down 1% due to outcomes-based agreements with payers like Optum. Gross-to-net was favorable at 22%, reflecting low rebate exposure in this cash-pay heavy segment. Ex-U.S. ASP averaged $1.6 million, with volume milestones offsetting tender pricing in the UK. Initiatives include viral vector CMC tech transfer to our Singapore facility for 20% COGS reduction by 2026 and a Phase 3 basket trial for HemoCure in other bleeding disorders. We're eyeing bolt-on M&A to double this franchise to $1.5 billion by 2027.

In aggregate, volume drove 10% of our 14% top-line growth, with pricing contributing 4% before headwinds. U.S. demand remains robust at 72% of sales, but ex-U.S. grew 20% year-over-year on 15% volume and flat pricing, aided by our 12-country access team. We're reaffirming FY24 net product sales growth of 13 to 16%, with oncology and rare diseases offsetting immunology normalization.

Turning to our operating expense analysis, total operating expenses for Q3 came in at $1.28 billion, up 18% year-over-year from $1.09 billion in Q3 2023. This was anticipated and primarily reflects accelerated R&D investments to advance our late-stage pipeline, including our lead asset AETHER-427, a next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody tracking toward BLA filing in the first half of 2025. Excluding a one-time $45 million milestone payment to Kyowa Kirin for CMC process validation, adjusted OpEx growth was 14%, aligning with guidance.

R&D expenses were $892 million, up 22% year-over-year and 70% of total OpEx, underscoring commitment to our 14 clinical-stage programs across oncology, rare diseases, and gene therapies. The increase stemmed from clinical trial ramp-up—we dosed first patients in the pivotal AETHER-427 STAR-3 trial in April, incurring $210 million in recruitment and site activation across 150 global sites, up 35% as we prioritize high-enrolling U.S. and EU sites. Technical initiatives took $165 million, or 18% of R&D, toward our AI-accelerated drug discovery platform leveraging PROTAC degraders, yielding two IND-ready candidates like a KRAS G12C degrader for pancreatic cancer. We're scaling viral vector manufacturing for GTX-789 with a new 50,000 L bioreactor in North Carolina, adding $75 million. U.S. R&D was $520 million, 58%; EMEA $250 million, 28%; APAC $122 million, 14% via WuXi Biologics. Headcount grew 12% to 2,450, with external spend flat at 42% of R&D.

SG&A expenses were $348 million, up 9% year-over-year and 27% of OpEx. This included $120 million in U.S. detailing and patient access for ZYN-214, our JAK inhibitor for RA capturing 8% share, with $40 million in co-pay assistance yielding 3.5x ROI. Headcount was flat at 1,200, with 5% G&A reduction via offshore finance and $15 million savings from digital marketing, shifting 30% HCP engagement virtual. U.S. SG&A $220 million, 63%; EU $85 million, 24%; APAC $43 million, 12%.

Other operating expenses were $40 million, up 5%, including $22 million in Irish facility expansions qualifying for 12.5% tax and $18 million in PROTAC IP litigation we view as value-accretive.

Trailing twelve-month OpEx as a percentage of revenue expanded to 82% from 75%, but we expect compression to 75% by year-end as revenues scale. Our R&D intensity at 5.2x revenue is competitive given our 70% Phase 2 success rate. Strategically, we terminated two early assets post-review, saving $80 million annually, reallocating to high-value programs; our AI platform cuts hit-to-lead by 40%; and 35% of R&D is low-cost sourced. We guide Q4 OpEx to $1.3 to $1.35 billion, full-year adjusted growth 15 to 17%.

Now, let's discuss our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities in more detail. For Q3, R&D expense was $428 million, up 12% year-over-year from $382 million, bringing trailing twelve-month spend to $1.72 billion, or 32% of revenue—above our 28 to 30% target but reflecting aggressive late-stage investments. Excluding stock comp and milestones, core R&D grew 9%, driven by trial enrollments and bispecific scale-up.

Oncology took 42% or $180 million, up 18%, fueled by next-gen ADCs and PROTACs. BPT-205, our lead HER2-directed ADC building on Enhertu and Trodelvy, progressed to Phase 3 TOPAZ-2 for frontline metastatic breast cancer, topline H2 2026, with $85 million including $25 million CMC for 5:1 DAR ratio potentially doubling PFS. BPT-472, PD-1/VEGF bispecific, advanced to Phase 2b combo.

Immunology and inflammation: 25% or $107 million, up 10%, emphasizing precision medicine. BPT-289 IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor hit 75% enrollment in Phase 3 psoriasis, targeting superiority over Tremfya, with $40 million in biomarker sub-studies using scRNA-seq cutting stratification by 40%.

Rare diseases and gene therapy: 18% or $77 million, up 22%, capitalizing on $20 billion market. BPT-GT7 AAV9 for DMD exon 51 skipping dosed first pediatric cohort, interim 35% dystrophin expression, with $30 million in NC viral production achieving 5x yields.

Early-stage: 15% or $64 million on AI discovery; $20 million in AlphaFold3-integrated platform nominating three neurodegeneration targets, cutting timelines from 24 to 12 months; $150 million CRISPR collab for base editing ALS.

Geographically, 55% U.S., 25% Europe with EMA PIP waivers, 20% APAC growing 25% via NMPA clearances and WuXi. We navigated IRA clawbacks at $50 million and biosimilar erosion on legacy TNF NovaLizumab losing 15% share via 8% discovery headcount cuts and 15% per-patient trial cost reductions using decentralized trials. Pipeline now 18 clinical assets, 70% Phase 2/3 across modalities.

FY24 R&D guided to $1.75 to $1.80 billion, Q4 $430 to $450 million. Milestones: BPT-GT7 interim Q1 2025, BPT-289 BLA mid-2025, two Phase 2 obesity starts.

Next, one of our most significant catalysts: regulatory approvals and label expansions. Our flagship AETHER-427, next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific, secured full FDA approval via BLA ahead of the May 15 PDUFA, for frontline metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1, based on Phase 3 AETHER-LUNG-301 showing 42% risk reduction vs. pembro monotherapy and 15% lower Grade 3+ irAEs. sNDA approval for second-line SCLC boosts U.S. TAM from $4.2 to $7.8 billion, unlocking $1.5 billion peak sales by 2028; Q3 U.S. sales ramping to $180 million, 250% QoQ, via NCCN Category 1.

EMA mirrored FDA/CHMP accelerated via PRIME, priced at €28,000/course, 10% below Tecentriq; Q4 EU launch for €450 million 2025 ex-U.S. sales. For NOVAzyme-19 AAV9 SMA Type 1, FDA expanded label to 21 kg from 13.5 kg on RWE and Phase 3 NOVA-SMA-202 with 92% event-free survival vs. 26% historical; U.S. pool up 35% to 610 infants, exclusivity to 2036.

Asia: PMDA label expansion for AETHER-427 EGFR-mutated NSCLC post-TKI, 38% ORR; NMPA supplemental for NOVAzyme-19 priority review. From adaptive designs—40% late-stage with Bayesian—and Roche PD-L1 IHC companion at 95% concordance. Triggered $350 million Takeda milestones, extending cash to 2028. Five more filings this year: AETHER-427 TNBC Phase 3 $3B TAM, NOVAzyme-19 SMA 2/3. These lift 2024 guidance $400 million to $1.8 to 2.0 billion revenue, margins +300 bps to 82%.

On the pricing and reimbursement landscape, critical for sustainability. U.S., 68% of revenues at $1.2 billion Q3, GTN 52% up from 49%, driven by rebates for NovaBlock PD-1 ($850 million U.S. sales), WAC $15,200/100mg vial, ASP 92% WAC via CMS RTOR RWE. IRA selects NovaRare-X for 2027 negotiation (2% pipeline); 340B discounts 45%; biosimilar erosion on HER2 ADC contained at 12% YTD via copay accumulators covering 78% patients <$25/month OOP.

Reimbursement wins: permanent J-code for NovaTrex-19 CAR-T in 85% centers; OBAs tying 15% NovaBlock to ORR/PFS, reversing $45 million rebates to revenue. Europe 22% revenues $390 million: Germany IQWiG "considerable benefit" AMNOG €12,500/cycle; 14/15 EU5 reimbursed, France HAS 98%; HTA reg addressed via pan-EU dossiers for NovaDual bispecific. Ex-China EM 11%, Brazil 105% WAC, Australia PBS A$14,200.

Globally, GTN erosion 3.2% YoY offset by AI pricing analytics with Komodo Health; value-based pilots for NovaTrex-19 reducing rebates 20%; $150 million patient access including NovaBridge 100% coverage under $100K boosting adherence 15%. For NovaGene-HA hemophilia BLA Q1 2025, pull-forward annuities $450K/year over 5-7 years. Amid GLP-1 constraints, metabolic-oncology combos eyed for $300 million peak. GTN to 54-56% next year, but 8-10% ASP growth 2025 via RWE/OBAs.

Before turning it back, key assumptions and risk factors for FY2024 guidance and outlook. Forward-looking subject to safe harbor; see 10-Q/10-K.

Key assumptions: GLP-1 portfolio $1.8 billion FY24, 25% growth, 12-14% TRx share via oral BPT-401, 65% adherence via Teladoc AI. Oncology $750 million, 18% growth, EU HTA for BPT-205 Q1 2025 €500 million peak, U.S. ASP $145K ASP, 28% GTN. U.S. 72% revenues, ex-U.S. +32% to $1.2 billion, Japan JPY 45 billion BPT-401, China 15% $5B GLP-1 via WuXi JV.

Pipeline: 58% PTS BPT-512 NASH Phase 3 Q4 2024, BLA BPT-401 combo mid-2025 85% PDUFA. R&D $2.1 billion 22% revenues, 40% AI DeepBio 20% Phase 1 attrition cut to 60%, capex $450 million Singapore.

Macro: 4-6% U.S. Medicare erosion offset 10% premium ultra-long GLP-1, ex-U.S. NICE/INESSS parity; $1.5 billion CRISPR milestones 75% prob.; EBITDA to 38% FY26 via digital SG&A 25% HCP Veeva, 82% margins post $300 million cost-out.

Risks: Clinical/reg: 20-30% BPT-512 miss -$1.2 billion NPV, 15% CRL BPT-205, REMS GLP-1 10-15% uptake cap.

Competitive/IP: 2026 LOE BPT-TNF1 70% $900 million cliff, Amgen/Samsung 40% share; Lilly orforglipron 5pt share loss; PTAB BPT-401 25% prob. to 2032.

Manufacturing: 10% revenue API shortages Lonza, dual-source <5% downtime; Devens Form 483 CMC delay.

Macro/geo: IRA 2027 BPT-401 25-60% price, PBM shifts 8% share; EU EMA delays 15%, China IP 10% JV growth; rates >4.5% +50bps $3.2 billion loan -$0.15 EPS; recession 20% CAR-T volumes -15%.

Strategic: 12% R&D turnover slips; ransomware 5% revenue 1-2 quarters.

Base embeds 60% confidence, stress-tested; mitigating via $500 million buyback, prioritization, fortress balance sheet net debt/EBITDA 1.2x.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, BPT-512 NASH asset is advancing with Phase 3 topline expected Q4 2024, AETHER-427 expansions in NSCLC/SCLC/TNBC on track, BPT-289 psoriasis enrollment at 75%, and BPT-GT7 DMD first cohort dosed with strong durability. Regulatory wins like FDA/EMA for AETHER-427 validate our adaptive designs and companions. We expect BLA submissions for BPT-401 combo mid-2025 and multiple readouts H1 2025.

Next, Dr. Raj Singh will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our DeepBio AI/ML platform is reducing Phase 1 attrition to 60% from industry 75%, nominating novel targets via AlphaFold3 in neurodegeneration and PROTACs. Advancements include KRAS degrader, bispecifics like PD-1/VEGF, and CRISPR base editing for ALS/hemophilia BPT-GT1, with partnerships yielding INDs and CMC optimizations like 5:1 DAR for ADCs. Our 18-asset pipeline is diversified 40% biologics, 30% small molecules, 20% cell/gene, 10% radiopharma.

Now I'll turn the call over to Karen Lee, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with $2.85 billion in net product sales up 14%. Strong uptake in OncoVita 28% NSCLC share, BPT-401 GLP-1 12-14% TRx stabilization, AETHER-427 ramp to $180 million post-labels, RariGene/HemoCure 35% volume surge. Marketing campaigns are proving effective in driving 20% NRx growth via digital HCP via Veeva 25% interactions, copay programs boosting adherence 15%, and 12-country access teams securing EU5/Germany/France reimbursements. U.S. 72% mix, ex-U.S. +20% on launches.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Karen. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the key risks, particularly Phase 3 for BPT-512 NASH and potential IRA impacts on BPT-401, how are you sensitivity-testing the guidance?

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thanks, John. Mike?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Sure, John. Our base case uses 58% PTS for BPT-512 based on LOESS/IQVIA benchmarks, with Monte Carlo sims showing a 20-30% topline miss shaving $1.2 billion NPV—we've stress-tested to -15% revenue adverse case with 60% confidence. For IRA 2027 on BPT-401, modeled 38% discount vs. 25-60% max, offset by premiums; overall conservative assumptions align with Evaluate Pharma consensus 4.2x FY26 $8.5 billion peak sales.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. On R&D spend priorities, with oncology at 42% and gene therapy up 22%, any shifts post-portfolio review, and FY24 guide details?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thanks, Emily. Post-review, terminated two early assets saving $80 million annually, ringfenced clinical dollars—oncology $180 million on BPT-205 Phase 3, gene $77 million BPT-GT7 with 5x yields. FY24 $1.75-1.80 billion, Q4 $430-450 million, accelerating H1 2025 on readouts like BPT-GT7 interim.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. For product revenues, oncology volumes up 13% but immunology softening—thoughts on biosimilar erosion and ex-U.S. growth?

Karen Lee, Head of Commercial:
Hi David. Oncology NRx +20% post-adjuvant label, combos +25%; immunology 8% volume but 5% TRx loss to TNF biosimilars, offset by Japan +18%. Ex-U.S. +20% on China/Japan launches, 15% volumes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Anna Kim, Barclays:
Thanks. Impressive regulatory wins on AETHER-427 labels—impact to 2025 sales and pipeline optionality?

Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Anna. AETHER-427 TAM to $7.8 billion U.S., €450 million ex-U.S. 2025; TNBC Phase 3 $3B TAM filing soon. Enhances M&A optionality like Regeneron/Checkmate, valued 12x 2028 peaks.

Operator:
Our next question from Mike Rodriguez with BofA. On pricing, GTN at 52%—how are OBAs and value-based models mitigating IRA/PBM pressures?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Good question, Mike. OBAs reversed $45 million Q3 on ORR/PFS; NovaBridge copays 78% coverage +15% adherence. Pioneering annuities for gene therapies $450K/year; AI analytics forecast 85% payer adherence, targeting 8-10% ASP growth 2025 despite 54-56% GTN.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the question-and-answer session.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the BioPharm Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
